verifications.claim: Satoshi Nakamoto is the pseudonymous creator(s) of Bitcoin.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator" (R1); "Satoshi Nakamoto is a pseudonym for the creator(s) of Bitcoin" (R2); "Bitcoin’s creator has hidden behind the pseudonym Satoshi Nakamoto" (R3); "pseudonymous creator of Bitcoin" (R5); "pseudonymous person or persons who developed bitcoin" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state Satoshi Nakamoto is the pseudonym for Bitcoin's creator(s).

verifications.claim: Satoshi Nakamoto published the original whitepaper in 2008.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "introduced the Bitcoin concept in a 2008 paper" (R2); "published the Bitcoin whitepaper in 2008" (R5); "On 31 October, Nakamoto published a white paper... 2008" (R6); "published a paper titled Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System... 2008" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of whitepaper publication in 2008 by Satoshi.

verifications.claim: Satoshi Nakamoto launched the network in 2009.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "launched the network in 2009" (R5); "On 9 January 2009, Nakamoto... launched the network" (R6); "released the Bitcoin platform to the public on January 3, 2009" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state network launch in 2009.

verifications.claim: Satoshi Nakamoto's true identity remains unknown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "whose identity remains unknown" (R2); "Bitcoin’s creator has hidden behind the pseudonym" (R3); "Satoshi's true identity remains unknown" (R5); "Nakamoto's true identity is unknown" (R6); "no one has confirmed the true identity" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: All sources affirm the identity is unknown.

verifications.claim: A 2026 investigation published by Fortune pointed to British cryptographer Adam Back as a likely candidate for Satoshi Nakamoto.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "Carreyrou claims... Satoshi Nakamoto is none other than British computer scientist Adam Back. It’s not a bad guess... but tripped up... confirmation bias" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: R8 (Fortune) reports on NYT's claim but criticizes and dismisses it as unproven, does not point to Back as likely candidate itself.

verifications.claim: The 2026 investigation published by Fortune aligns with a New York Times report.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "The New York Times says it found Satoshi... Not so fast"; "confirmation bias is what tripped up... Carreyrou as well" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Fortune article explicitly contradicts and criticizes the NYT report.

verifications.claim: Adam Back is a British cryptographer.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "British cryptographer who invented Hashcash" (R1); "55-year-old computer scientist named Adam Back" (R3); "55-year-old Adam Back — the CEO of Blockstream, a prominent cryptographer" (R4); "Adam Back, inventor of bitcoin predecessor Hashcash" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as British cryptographer across sources.

verifications.claim: Satoshi Nakamoto vanished in April 2011.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "last known communication was in April 2011" (R5); "fl. 31 October 2008 – 26 April 2011" (R6); "disappeared in April 2011" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Specific date of vanishing in April 2011 confirmed.

verifications.claim: Satoshi Nakamoto stepped back from the project.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Nakamoto’s involvement with Bitcoin... ended in 2010"; "moved on to other things" (R2); "he had “moved on to other things,”" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements of stepping back/moving on.

verifications.claim: Satoshi Nakamoto is believed to hold approximately 1.1 million Bitcoins.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Satoshi has about 1 million BTC... between 750 bitcoin and 1.1 million bitcoin" (R2); "estimated to hold approximately 1.1 million Bitcoin" (R5); "holds an estimated 1.1 million bitcoins" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Exact figure of ~1.1 million consistently attributed to Satoshi.

verifications.claim: Satoshi Nakamoto's approximately 1.1 million Bitcoins have never been moved.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "these coins have never been moved since 2010" (R5); "His wallet, which has been untouched since 2010" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Satoshi's coins unmoved since 2010.

verifications.claim: Satoshi Nakamoto's approximately 1.1 million Bitcoins are worth over $125 billion.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "worth over $125 billion at current prices" (R5); "At their July 14, 2025 price... nearly $135 billion" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: R5 directly states over $125B; R6 similar value, slightly higher.

verifications.claim: Proposed candidates for Satoshi Nakamoto's identity include Hal Finney, Nick Szabo, and Adam Back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Hal Finney... Nick Szabo" (R2); "Back is considered one of the more plausible candidates along with... Hal Finney and Nick Szabo" (R4); "Adam Back... Hal Finney... Nick Szabo" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: All three named as candidates in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: According to Wikipedia, no one has been definitively proven to be Satoshi Nakamoto.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Nakamoto's true identity is unknown"; lists candidates but notes denials and no proof
verifications.reasoning: Wikipedia explicitly states identity unknown, no definitive proof.

verifications.claim: A detailed investigation was led by journalist John Carreyrou.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "John Carreyrou... spent 18 months trying to identify" (R1); "John Carreyrou spent a year digging" (R3); "John Carreyrou — the author of the investigation" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Carreyrou led the NYT investigation.

verifications.claim: John Carreyrou suggested that Adam Back, the CEO of Blockstream, is Satoshi Nakamoto.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "His conclusion... Adam Back... CEO" (R1); "identifies... Adam Back — the CEO of Blockstream" (R4); "John Carreyrou... suggesting he could be Satoshi Nakamoto" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Carreyrou's investigation concludes/suggests Back is Satoshi.

verifications.claim: Adam Back is the CEO of Blockstream.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Back has co-founded... As CEO" (R1); "Adam Back — the CEO of Blockstream" (R4); "CEO of Blockstream" implied in context (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: John Carreyrou's investigation cited linguistic analysis showing similar nonstandard hyphenation errors in early emails and forum posts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Carreyrou ran Satoshi's hyphenation errors — 325 instances of nonstandard usage — against 620 writers... Back matched 67"
verifications.reasoning: R1 details the exact hyphenation analysis in Carreyrou's work.

verifications.claim: Adam Back’s early work was on Hashcash.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "British cryptographer who invented Hashcash" (R1); "proof-of-work system designed by Adam Back" (R2); "Back’s early work on Hashcash" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently attributed to Back.

verifications.claim: Hashcash is the proof-of-work system used by Bitcoin.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Hashcash, the computational puzzle system that became Bitcoin's proof-of-work mining engine" (R1); "using something similar to the proof-of-work system designed by Adam Back" (R2); "Hashcash, a proof-of-work system crucial for bitcoin mining" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm Hashcash as Bitcoin's PoW basis.

verifications.claim: A New York Times investigation reported a decrease in Adam Back's online activity during the period Satoshi Nakamoto was active.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Back went nearly silent on the Cryptography mailing list during the years Satoshi was active" (R1); "Back's reduced activity on cryptography mailing lists during the period Nakamoto was active" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: NYT investigation specifically notes Back's decreased activity.

verifications.claim: Adam Back has denied being the creator.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Back has denied it" (R1); "Back has denied various claims... he is not Satoshi Nakamoto" (R4); "Back denied being Nakamoto multiple times" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm Back's denials.
